item.name: OAuth 2.0
item.description:
Google Health API's authorization-code flow as its documentation describes it, read 2026-11-05. Fill client_id, redirect_uri and scope in an environment of your own and keep client_secret there, never in a shared collection.

The same facts, with each source sentence, at https://aifitnessapi.com/google-health-api and https://aifitnessapi.com/tools/oauth-playground.

request.description:
https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth. Google's OAuth 2.0 authorization endpoint (HTTPS only). Open this URL in a browser (in Postman: copy it from the request bar); the user signs in and Google Health API redirects to {{redirect_uri}} with ?code=… Put that value in the auth_code variable.

Source: Google Identity, “Using OAuth 2.0 for Web Server Applications”, https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/web-server

Scope: Space-separated full scope URLs. The Google Health API's scopes are listed with Google's consent wording; add prompt=consent when you change them. Source: Google Health API, “Set up Google Cloud and OAuth”, https://developers.google.com/health/setup

Documented scopes (joined with spaces):
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.activity_and_fitness.readonly: See your Google Health activity and fitness data.
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.activity_and_fitness.writeonly: Add activity and fitness data to Google Health, and edit or delete the data it adds.
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.ecg.readonly: See your Google Health ECG data.
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.health_metrics_and_measurements.readonly: See your Google Health health metrics and measurement data.
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.health_metrics_and_measurements.writeonly: Add health metric and measurements data to Google Health, and edit or delete the data it adds.
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.irn.readonly: See your Google Health Irregular Rhythm Notifications data.
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.location.readonly: See your Google Health GPS location recorded during an exercise.
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.logged_symptoms.writeonly: Add logged symptoms data to Google Health, and edit or delete the data it adds.
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.mindfulness.writeonly: Add mindfulness data to Google Health, and edit or delete the data it adds.
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.nutrition.readonly: See your Google Health nutrition data.
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.nutrition.writeonly: Add nutrition data to Google Health, and edit or delete the data it adds.
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.profile.readonly: See your Google Health profile data.
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.profile.writeonly: Add profile data to Google Health, and edit or delete the data it adds.
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.reproductive_health.writeonly: Add reproductive health data to Google Health, and edit or delete the data it adds.
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.settings.readonly: See your Google Health settings.
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.settings.writeonly: Add settings data to Google Health, and edit or delete the data it adds.
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.sleep.readonly: See your Google Health sleep data.
- https://www.googleapis.com/auth/googlehealth.sleep.writeonly: Add sleep data to Google Health, and edit or delete the data it adds.

Source: Google Health API, “Scopes” (via this site's generated Google Health API dataset), https://developers.google.com/health/scopes

PKCE: Not described on Google's web-server OAuth page, which this tool follows.

https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token. Token URL, for the exchange and refresh.

Source: Google Identity, “Using OAuth 2.0 for Web Server Applications”, https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/web-server

Client credentials go in the form body.

Token lifetime: expires_in gives the remaining lifetime in seconds; Google's sample shows 3920. Source: Google Identity, “Using OAuth 2.0 for Web Server Applications”, https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/web-server

Note: access_type=offline is what makes Google return a refresh token. Source: Google Identity, “Using OAuth 2.0 for Web Server Applications”, https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/web-server

Note: Google limits refresh tokens per client/user pair and per user. Source: Google Identity, “Using OAuth 2.0 for Web Server Applications”, https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/web-server

Note: A new OAuth client is unverified and capped at 100 users, each added as a test user. Source: Google Health API, “Set up Google Cloud and OAuth”, https://developers.google.com/health/setup

Refresh: access_type=offline gets a refresh token on the first exchange only. Refresh tokens last until revoked or expired, and Google caps how many it issues per client and user.

Source: Google Identity, “Using OAuth 2.0 for Web Server Applications”, https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/web-server

item.name: Webhook samples
item.description:
Google Health API's documented example notifications, sent to {{local_url}} (your local handler) unchanged. Signature: Google sends the endpointAuthorization secret you configured in the Authorization header. It also signs the raw JSON with Tink (ECDSA P-256, SHA-256), base64 in GOOGLE-HEALTH-API-SIGNATURE, keys rotated every 30 days and published as a JSON keyset. Source: Google Health API, “Webhook subscriptions”, https://developers.google.com/health/webhooks

Headers that carry a signature hold the placeholder Google Health API prints, so a handler that verifies signatures will reject these: to send correctly signed requests, use https://aifitnessapi.com/webhooks/send-sample.mjs. Respond: Validate the Authorization header and respond 204 No Content immediately; process asynchronously. On subscriber create or endpoint change, two POSTs with {"type": "verification"}: answer the authorized one with 200 or 201 and the unauthenticated one with 401 or 403.

Payload library with JSON Schemas: https://aifitnessapi.com/webhooks#google-health.
